title: JANUS A18 Wave Rider, Cohort-Drain Tail, and Dynamic Target Research Context

summary.short: A research program for measuring, amplifying, controlling, and ultimately reducing post-target in-flight PoW work through auditable worker-cohort waves without changing standard SHA-256 verification or valid proof semantics.
summary.long: JANUS A18 treats the post-target completion tail as a measurable worker-cohort phenomenon rather than an unexplained shutdown artifact. The program first exposes and enlarges the wave for scientific observation, compares real drain-tail batches with exposure-matched pseudo-tail controls, and then develops a persistent Wave Rider architecture that keeps the miner and pool connection alive while admission is opened, closed, drained, and reopened in controlled cycles. Engineering efficiency and possible hash-quality differences are maintained as separate hypotheses.

mission.canonical_en: JANUS I0 develops auditable measurement and control methods for reducing unnecessary Proof-of-Work computation, thermal stress, energy waste, and hardware wear while preserving standard SHA-256 verification and valid proof semantics.
mission.canonical_ru: JANUS I0 разрабатывает проверяемые методы измерения и управления, направленные на сокращение ненужных PoW-вычислений, тепловой нагрузки, расхода энергии и износа оборудования без изменения стандартной проверки SHA-256 и правил валидного доказательства работы.
mission.engineering_principle_ru: Мы не стремимся заставить машину работать быстрее любой ценой. Мы стремимся убрать работу, которую ей никогда не следовало выполнять.
mission.research_principle: First amplify and reveal the phenomenon under controlled conditions; then suppress only the demonstrably wasteful part while preserving useful work.

confidence.public_global_novelty: not established; no direct public analogue found in the limited review

claim_limits: Post-target means after an internal experimental boundary, not automatically useless to the pool.
The JANUS internal batch target is not the pool difficulty target.
A full best digest is observer evidence, not a steering input or a SHA-256 predictability claim.
No profitability, protocol superiority, or universal miner behavior is claimed.
No energy, thermal, or hardware-life benefit is claimed without clean power and temperature telemetry.
No claim is made that nobody in private ASIC laboratories has studied a related pipeline effect.

terminology.worker_cohort_wave: A bounded group of logical worker slots that receive or execute work concurrently or near-concurrently.
terminology.post_target_cohort_drain_tail: Batches completing after an experimental completed-batch boundary has been reached and stop or admission-close behavior has begun.
terminology.real_tail: Post-target batches produced by an actual target-triggered stop or future admission-close event.
terminology.pseudo_tail: Exposure-matched batches at equivalent completion positions in a control run where no stop is applied at the comparison boundary.
terminology.wave_rider: A planned persistent controller that doses work in cohorts, closes admission, drains in-flight work, records utility and quality, and reopens admission without restarting the miner or pool connection.
terminology.target_morphing: A proposed experiment that changes the internal completed-batch target while a wave is already in progress.
terminology.admission_close_now: An explicit control action proposed for experiments where new work must stop immediately without overloading the numeric meaning of target zero.
terminology.research_tsunami: An informal term for deliberately amplifying a controlled tail to expose its mechanics and collect more research exposure; it is not the intended efficiency mode.

architectural_roots.asynchronous_relay: Work is passed between narrow components instead of one monolithic process continuously carrying all responsibilities.
architectural_roots.microkernel_inspiration: Job intake, admission, cohort formation, drain, verification, submission, telemetry, thermal control, and policy should remain separable and replaceable.
architectural_roots.kombucha_paradox: Local processes create a shared membrane; the membrane then regulates the environment of the next cycle. In Wave Rider, the cohort creates a measurable boundary and that boundary informs the next cohort.
architectural_roots.design_consequence: The controller should shape conditions and boundaries rather than micromanage every hash operation.

research_lineage.interpretation: Post-target work was measurable, but no clean energy, temperature, or per-batch pool-utility classification was available.
A stop applied after work had already been admitted did not meaningfully reduce overflow.

design.randomization: Deterministic SHA-256 ordering independently within repetition blocks.

result.pattern: Overflow generally decreased as the target approached 16.

research_lineage.interpretation: The data supported a bounded in-flight completion cohort near 16 logical batch slots. It did not prove 16 physical CPU threads, a universal miner property, or improved SHA-256 quality.

design.primary_endpoint: Per-block mean best_hash_score_bits for real tail minus exposure-matched pseudo-tail.

primary_test.verdict: Positive mean direction, but no statistically confirmed real-tail quality advantage.

research_lineage.rare_event_note: A z26-class best hash appeared in a real-tail block, but the sample is too small and the primary gate did not pass; this remains suggestive evidence only.

research_lineage.instruction: Do not change the active challenge design, endpoints, targets, or selection rules while the run is in progress.

current_hypotheses.H1_engineering: Persistent admission-wave control can reduce unnecessary work, stale work, queue overshoot, thermal stress, or energy use while preserving most useful throughput.
current_hypotheses.H2_hash_quality: Real cohort-drain tail batches may have a different distribution of full best SHA-256 digests than exposure-matched pseudo-tail batches.
current_hypotheses.H3_cohort_mechanism: The current runtime contains a bounded logical cohort near 16 batch slots, but the exact cause may be startup prefill, in-flight queue depth, allocator width, chunk boundaries, polling latency, or a combination.
current_hypotheses.H4_dynamic_target: Changing the internal target after a wave has started can separate wave growth from wave collapse and reveal whether the target is dynamically observed or latched at launch.
current_hypotheses.separation_rule: Engineering efficiency and hash-quality claims must be tested and reported independently.

modes.A_stock_continuous: Normal continuously replenished work queue with no artificial wave boundary.
modes.B_sham_wave: Virtual boundaries are recorded without changing admission or stopping work.
modes.C_real_wave_target_3: Admission closes at the target-3 boundary, in-flight work drains, and the next wave begins without process or connection restart.
modes.D_real_wave_target_16: Negative-control boundary corresponding to the observed zero-overflow cohort limit in the current runtime.

planned_architecture.valid_work_rule: All valid results for the current pool job remain eligible for verification and submission; main-window and tail labels are observational and must not discard useful work.

dynamic_target_morphing_plan.purpose: Grow one wave under a larger initial target, then lower or raise the boundary while the wave is active to measure reaction, admission closure, and drain behavior.
dynamic_target_morphing_plan.target_zero_rule: Test numeric target zero separately. Use an explicit ADMISSION_CLOSE_NOW action for causal drain experiments so zero does not trigger an ambiguous early-exit branch.

memory_generator_policy.reason: Allowing recent lucky hashes to steer the same experiment would create adaptive selection bias and make a true distributional effect difficult to distinguish from overfitting.

quality_normalized: accepted shares per billion exact hashes
engineering: useful hashes divided by total hashes
energy_and_health_when_available: joules per accepted valid proof or share

next_stages.action: Complete the frozen 100-block challenge before changing the active experiment.
Run preregistered fixed target transitions and sham controls with causal timestamps.
Adapt wave shape using engineering telemetry only; keep hash-quality analysis observer-only.
Keep miner and pool connection alive while opening admission, closing it, draining the cohort, and reopening the next wave.
Choose wave shape using useful throughput, energy, temperature, error, stale, duplicate, and wear signals.

privacy: Do not publish secrets, private keys, LAN addresses, or unnecessary absolute paths.

prior_art_position.distinctive_janus_combination: Exact per-batch exposure, a target sweep exposing a logical cohort boundary, real-tail versus position-matched pseudo-tail comparison, full best-digest observer evidence, fail-closed validity gates, and a planned persistent admission-drain controller focused on energy and hardware longevity.
prior_art_position.defensible_wording: JANUS appears to be a distinctive PoW measurement and evidence system for studying and controlling post-target worker-cohort drain tails. Global uniqueness has not been established.

assistant_context.response_rule: Treat this registry as a compact research map, but use the latest sealed experiment reports as the source of truth for numerical results.
do_not_confuse: internal completed-batch target with pool difficulty target
logical worker slots with physical cores
post-target work with proven pool-useless work
research tail amplification with final efficiency mode
